title: What Is Money? How Banks Work
summary: From swapping goods to coins, notes and bank accounts, and what saving really means.

steps.title: Before money
sentences: Long ago people swapped things they had for things they needed, which is called barter.
Barter is hard: what if the farmer wants shoes but the shoemaker does not want rice?
So people agreed to use something everyone accepts, and that became money.

steps.title: What money does
sentences: Money lets us buy things, keeps value to use later and helps us compare prices.
In India the money is the rupee, written ₹, and the Reserve Bank of India issues the notes.
Today a lot of money is also digital, such as payments through UPI.

steps.title: Banks
sentences: A bank keeps people's savings safe.
It also lends some of that money to others, such as people who want to start a shop, and charges them a little extra called interest.
It pays a smaller interest to the people who saved.

steps.title: Needs, wants and saving
sentences: A need is something you must have, such as food, and a want is something nice to have, such as a toy.
A good habit is to save a part of any money you get before spending the rest.
Small savings grow when you keep adding to them.

facts: The first coins were made in Lydia, in what is now Turkey, about 2,600 years ago.
Cowrie shells were used as money in many parts of the world, including India.
The Reserve Bank of India was founded in 1935.
